findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 2: scaffold.py:345-349 reads bytes, decodes with errors="replace", catches OSError; test_a_readme_that_predates_utf8 fails on abc8c66
findings.message: `read_text` on the README is guarded only against a missing file: a README in cp1251 or latin-1 raises UnicodeDecodeError and `aegis init` exits 3 with "this is a bug in aegis", where the previous commit's init succeeded on the same repository. The first command of the first hour aborts on a brownfield project whose README predates UTF-8.
findings.minimal_fix: catch UnicodeDecodeError around the read (or decode with errors="replace") and fall through to the no-README text

findings.message: The `cli` step's note says `aegis init` "keeps every answer", but a plain re-run on a project initialised with `--yes` drops `accepted_assumptions`, rebuilds the ledger and flips status complete→provisional, so the step after the constitution is "review the assumption ledger [human]" (verified: 5 rows, `next` says human). The wait R-33 removed comes back one step later, from the framework's own advice, and `next --run` executes it unattended; the test at :1334 never asserts the status afterwards.
findings.minimal_fix: advise `aegis scaffold` (writes only the missing files, leaves answers.json byte-identical — verified) and change the assertion at tests/test_aegis.py:1338, or carry `accepted_assumptions` and `status` over in `initialise` on a non-`--force` re-run and lock it

findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 2: checks.py:1388 warns on the template; flow.py:1702-1705 sends a missing constitution to `aegis init` (its side effect is the new sev-3)
findings.message: `check_setup` still fails the task gate on a `<one paragraph` constitution while `next` no longer names it: a project initialised by the previous version keeps its template (`put_text` leaves an existing file without --force), `next` sends it through spec, task and build, and the task gate then stops on "a human writes its purpose". That is the wait R-33 forbids, moved after the work, with `next` and the gate disagreeing; with the file deleted outright, `next` likewise says "specify the first feature" and `check_structure` fails "constitution.md is missing".
findings.minimal_fix: drop the template check in check_setup (or make it warn), and have `next` say "run aegis init" when constitution.md is absent

findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 2: detect.py:429 `^@?`; test_a_quiet_just_recipe_is_a_target fails on abc8c66
findings.message: JUST_RECIPE requires a letter or underscore at column 0, so a quiet recipe `@test:` (the common `just` idiom for suppressing echo) is not a target; with `lint:` matched, the inferred `pytest -q` is popped and the package has no test command at all. The gate on a code-only task runs `just lint` and verifies nothing.

The header (with flow.py:381 and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:56) promises an agent may amend the constitution "only through a task", but `_task_new_locked` at flow.py:142-148 refuses every `.aegis/` glob, so `task new --owns .aegis/constitution.md` is refused (verified). An agent following the sentence either stops for a person or edits outside any lease, where `check trace` skips ownerless `.aegis/` paths silently; R-33's own text carries the wording, so the disagreement is spec versus flow.py:145.
findings.minimal_fix: exempt `.aegis/constitution.md` from the framework-state refusal in `_task_new_locked`, or (owner) reword R-33 and the three sentences to "a person amends it; an agent proposes the change"

findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 2: detect.py:352-354 pops the inferred keys only when the front door defines `test`; R-34 amended; test fails on abc8c66
findings.message: Popping all four inferred keys whenever the front door defines any of them: a Go project with a Makefile of `build` and `clean` loses the `go test ./...` and `go vet ./...` the previous code kept, so code-only tasks pass with only `make build` run (the "no command ran" guard is silent) and tasks touching tests fail "no package declares a test command". This is R-34's literal wording, so the owner decides whether "replace" means the set or the key.
findings.minimal_fix: pop the inferred keys only when the front door defines `test`; a front door with only `build` has said nothing about tests

findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 2: scaffold.py:371-383 handles every shape named (HTML block, fence with blank line, shared heading, BOM, lists, quotes, comments), locked by the seven-case test; setext and bold-lead are new findings
findings.message:
The prose filter is a prefix list, so the purpose becomes `

` on an HTML badge block, `widgets run ```` when a fenced block contains a blank line, `pip install widgets` when the heading and the description share a paragraph, and `\ufeff# Widgets` on a BOM'd README; numbered lists, blockquotes and `` are taken too. The file is labelled a draft, but until a person rewrites it every agent reads that line as the project's purpose.
findings.minimal_fix: strip leading `#` lines and a BOM inside a paragraph, skip paragraphs starting with `<`, `>` or a digit, and skip everything until an opened fence closes

findings.message:
A setext underline is not stripped from the paragraph, so `Widgets
=======` drafts the purpose as "Widgets =======" (verified), and `Widgets
=======
Widgets turns…` as "Widgets ======= Widgets turns…". Every `README.rst` — a name the function tries — has an underlined title, so each one gets the wrong guess the docstring says costs more than an empty one.
findings.minimal_fix: drop lines matching `^(=+|-+|~+)\s*$` (and `^\.\. ` directives) when building `lines`, before the prefix test

findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 2: detect.py:432 JUSTFILE_NAMES includes .justfile; test fails on abc8c66
findings.message: `just` also reads `.justfile`; that spelling is not a front door here, so such a project gets exactly the R-34 friction (`mypy .` proposed from pyproject).

findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 2: README.md:251-253 says CLAUDE.md and the AGENTS.md chain warn, skills and roles fail
findings.message: "Known limits" still says the bootstrap budgets — CLAUDE.md, the AGENTS.md chain — fail because they are loaded into every session; since R-32 both warn. The README now promises a gate the code no longer applies.
findings.minimal_fix: say CLAUDE.md and the AGENTS.md chain warn, skills and roles still fail

findings.message: `*` in the skip list conflates a list marker with leading emphasis, so `**Widgets** turns orders into invoices.` is skipped and the next paragraph — verified as `pip install widgets` after its heading is stripped — becomes the purpose. A bold project name is a common first paragraph.
findings.minimal_fix: skip a list only on `re.match(r"[-*+]\s", lines[0])`, keeping the bare-prefix test for the other markers

findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 2: __main__.py:299 and :307 no longer say to write it by hand
findings.message: `init`'s closing advice still says "write .aegis/constitution.md by hand — it is the one file agents never touch" (and `scaffold` says "edit … by hand" at 307), while the file it just wrote says it was drafted by the agent and needs no one. The first thing an adopter reads after init contradicts R-33.
findings.minimal_fix: "1. read .aegis/constitution.md — drafted from the README; amend it whenever you like"

findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 2: tests/test_aegis.py:1307 asserts `next` on the drafted file via clear_human_gates(constitution=False)
findings.message: The `next` assertion runs after `clear_human_gates()` has replaced the constitution with "A fixture.", so it passes with the deleted step restored; the test fails on the old code through its earlier assertions, but the "next has no constitution step" half of R-33 has no lock.
findings.minimal_fix: assert `next` before clear_human_gates, on the init-drafted constitution (or with the file removed)

findings.message: `errors="replace"` keeps init alive, but the test's own cp1251 README drafts a purpose that is 54 U+FFFD out of 64 characters (verified), and the file says it was drafted from the README. Every agent reads a line of replacement characters as the project's purpose until a person notices.
findings.minimal_fix: if "\ufffd" in purpose, fall through to the no-README text (or try cp1251 before replacing)
